seed_ideas.title: MD verification inserted into Org-Mol's ester shortlist before synthesis
seed_ideas.text: Data-centre immersion cooling needs dielectric liquids with low viscosity, high thermal conductivity and heat capacity, and PFAS rules are pushing the field towards PFAS-free esters. Restrict the generative search to synthetically accessible PFAS-free esters of the kind already ML-screened at scale, filter to a ranked shortlist, and MD-verify the top 100, 300 then 1000 candidates' viscosity and thermal conductivity before any synthesis decision. Score against measured data for known esters and commercial single-phase fluids held out of training, never against the predictors. More compute buys more MD-verified candidates and longer simulations per candidate, testing whether the best cooling figure of merit keeps climbing beyond the 461-candidate shortlist stage.
seed_ideas.root_question: generative pipeline for discovery of single phase immersion coolants
seed_ideas.root_link: SAME: ester discovery kept on transport properties and on the down-selection step where prior work stops.
seed_ideas.compute_open: MD-verified candidates (100–1000, anchored to a ~461-candidate shortlist) and simulation length per candidate. Unknown: whether MD meaningfully reorders an ML shortlist or merely confirms it.
seed_ideas.changes: Changes the system studied: esters only, inside a synthetically accessible space, instead of esters plus hydrocarbons, with the candidate count anchored to the existing 461-candidate shortlist. Answers the gap that the Org-Mol/SINOPEC team ML-filtered millions of esters but manually picked only two to synthesise and never MD-verified the shortlist; also partially probes whether the best figure of merit still improves from ~100 to ~1000 verified candidates.
